notes:
Also written as {郭|くるわ}. Has two distinct historical meanings that share the concept of an enclosed, walled-off area.

PLEASURE QUARTER USAGE:
Refers to the walled entertainment districts of the Edo period (1603-1868) where licensed prostitution operated. The most famous was {吉原|よしわら} in Edo (modern Tokyo). These districts developed rich cultural traditions including distinctive speech patterns ({廓|くるわ}⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧), fashion, music, and art that influenced Japanese literature and kabuki theater.

CASTLE USAGE:
In castle architecture, {廓|くるわ} (or {曲輪|くるわ}) refers to the enclosed areas within a castle's defensive walls. Castles typically had multiple {廓|くるわ}: the ⟦{本丸|ほんまる}→本丸：24197_honmaru⟧ (main compound), {二|に}の{丸|まる} (second compound), and {三|さん}の{丸|まる} (third compound).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{遊郭|ゆうかく}→遊郭：15373_yuukaku⟧: pleasure quarter — a more common reading/writing, specifically for the entertainment district sense
- ⟦{花街|かがい}→花街：17224_kagai⟧: geisha quarter — a district of teahouses and geisha entertainment, distinct from {廓|くるわ}
- {曲輪|くるわ}: bailey, compound — the castle-specific spelling
